evidence.text: The dictionary says 你 is a singular second-person pronoun, absent from oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions and from Shuowen. It cites 集韻·止韻 (“你，汝也”) and 隋書·李密傳 (“共你論相殺事”), then notes its common use as a singular second-person pronoun in later Chinese. This supports an attested use by the time of the text, but does not by itself date the wording of the passage to the events it narrates.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 你

evidence.field: 說文釋形、字樣說明、釋義
evidence.text: The entry says 你 is not included in Shuowen and describes its right component as 尔. It records 你, “汝也,” in 集韻, and quotes a second-person use from 周書·卷五〇·異域列傳下·突厥. It also lists later plural, possessive, and generic uses. Those later meanings should not be treated as a chronology without dated contextual evidence.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》：你

evidence.text: For 尔, the dictionary describes the bronze form as a truncation of the upper part of 爾 and calls 尔 a shortened form of 爾. It says 尔/爾 was used for ‘you/your’ and later developed into modern Mandarin 你. This is an account of 尔 and its word history, not direct proof that 尔 names an independently pronounced depicted object. In a proposed 你 compound, the sound role of 尔 must be assessed separately from this whole-character historical relationship.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 尔

evidence.field: 字形資料; 甲骨、金文、小篆
evidence.text: The 尔 entry displays one small-seal and two bronze examples, and no oracle-bone examples. Its text describes the bronze shape as a shortened form of 爾. No inspected source here establishes an original depicted object or recoverable object-name pronunciation for 尔; therefore an object-based account of a whole-graph loan is unsupported by this evidence.

gaps: The retrieved primary-style dictionary accounts support a 亻 semantic component and are compatible with 尔 as sound element, but no independently inspected paleographic source in this pass directly analyzes 你 as a phono-semantic compound. The dossier's competing ideographic analysis is not established by the inspected evidence.

No original depicted object or independent historical pronunciation for 尔 as an object-name was established. This limits an object-based whole-graph borrowing proposal; it does not by itself disprove 尔's proposed phonetic role in 你.

The earliest surviving attestation of the written graph 你 was not established. CUHK reports absence from oracle and bronze inscriptions and Shuowen, and cites 集韻 and 隋書; the exact first attestation and textual transmission dating need specialist source verification.

No dated evidence in this pass establishes a semantic bridge from second-person singular to plural, possessive, or generic uses; MOE records such examples, while CUHK distinguishes older uses of 爾/尔 from the later use of 你.

No external reading comparison for both 你 and 尔 within a single historical reconstruction system was verified. Dossier readings *nɯʔ and *njelʔ are secondary-source claims and should not be repeated as independently checked here; current 尔 kMandarin was not verified.
